description: This topic covers practical writing formats such as letters, reports, CVs, memos, notices, agendas, minutes, forms, invitations and short messages, and how to choose the right layout, language and register for a given purpose and audience.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best defines functional writing?

options.text: Writing that entertains readers with imaginative stories
Writing done for a practical, everyday purpose using set formats
Writing poems that follow strict rhyme schemes
Writing personal diaries that no one else reads

mcq.explanation: Functional writing serves real-life practical purposes, such as letters, reports and memos, and follows recognised formats and conventions.

mcq.questionText: Which heading is NOT part of a standard memorandum (memo)?

options.text: To
From
Subject
Yours faithfully

mcq.explanation: A memo uses the headings To, From, Date and Subject. 'Yours faithfully' is a closing phrase used in formal letters, not in memos.

mcq.questionText: In a formal letter that begins with 'Dear Sir,', which closing is correct?

options.text: Yours faithfully,
Yours sincerely,
Lots of love,
See you soon,

mcq.explanation: When a formal letter opens with 'Dear Sir/Madam' (name unknown), it closes with 'Yours faithfully'. 'Yours sincerely' is used only when the recipient's name is used in the greeting.

mcq.questionText: Which document is written to give a detailed account of an investigation or event, organised under headings such as introduction, findings and recommendations?

options.text: A notice
A report
A telegram
An invitation card

mcq.explanation: A report presents organised information about an event or investigation and typically includes a title, introduction, findings, conclusion and recommendations.

mcq.questionText: What is the main purpose of a curriculum vitae (CV)?

options.text: To invite friends to a birthday party
To summarise a person's education, skills and work experience for a job
To record what was said at a meeting
To announce a public event

mcq.explanation: A CV gives an employer a summary of an applicant's personal details, education, qualifications, work experience and skills.

mcq.questionText: Which item is usually written DURING a meeting to record decisions and discussions?

options.text: Agenda
Minutes
Notice of meeting
Application letter

mcq.explanation: Minutes are the written record of what was discussed and decided during a meeting. The agenda and notice are prepared before the meeting.

mcq.questionText: An agenda is best described as:

options.text: A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
A summary of a person's qualifications
A short urgent message sent by post
A record of who attended a meeting

mcq.explanation: An agenda is the ordered list of topics or items to be dealt with at a meeting, circulated beforehand.

mcq.questionText: Which feature is most typical of a telegram or short message?

options.text: Long, detailed sentences with many adjectives
Brief wording that leaves out non-essential words to save space
Several body paragraphs and a formal closing
A table of contents and page numbers

mcq.explanation: Telegrams and short messages are kept very brief; small words like articles are often omitted so that only the essential message remains.

mcq.questionText: A friend writes to tell you about her holiday and asks how your family is. What type of letter is this?

options.text: An informal (personal) letter
A formal application letter
A memorandum
A business circular

mcq.explanation: A letter between friends about personal matters is an informal letter, which uses a relaxed and friendly tone.

mcq.questionText: When choosing a format for a piece of writing, the most important consideration is:

options.text: The colour of the paper used
The purpose of the writing and the intended audience
How long the writer has been at school
The number of words the writer can spell

mcq.explanation: The correct format and register depend on why you are writing (purpose) and who will read it (audience).

mcq.questionText: Which of these is a notice?

options.text: A private letter to a relative
A public message on a board informing students that the library will close early
A list of a person's referees
A signed record of a meeting's decisions

mcq.explanation: A notice is a short, clear public message displayed to inform many people about something, such as a change in opening hours.

mcq.questionText: Which closing phrase is appropriate for an informal letter to a close friend?

options.text: Yours faithfully
Yours sincerely
Your loving friend
Respectfully submitted

mcq.explanation: Informal letters use warm, personal closings such as 'Your loving friend', 'Yours ever' or 'With love'. The other phrases are formal.

mcq.questionText: An application letter sent together with a CV is best written in which register?

options.text: Casual and humorous
Formal and polite
Slang and abbreviations
Emotional and exaggerated

mcq.explanation: Application letters address an employer and must use formal, polite and professional language to create a good impression.

mcq.questionText: In the minutes of a meeting, 'apologies' usually refers to:

options.text: Members saying sorry for arguing
The names of members who could not attend and sent word in advance
Corrections made to the previous minutes
A vote of thanks at the end of the meeting

mcq.explanation: In meeting minutes, 'apologies' lists the members who were unable to attend and who informed the secretary or chairperson beforehand.

mcq.questionText: When filling in an official form, the BEST practice is to:

options.text: Write long descriptive paragraphs in every box
Follow the instructions and give only the information requested, neatly and accurately
Leave most spaces blank to save time
Use nicknames and informal abbreviations

mcq.explanation: Forms should be completed by following the given instructions exactly, writing clearly and supplying accurate, relevant details in the spaces provided.

fib.questionText: A formal letter that opens with 'Dear Madam,' should close with 'Yours _____,'.
fib.explanation: When the recipient's name is not used, the correct closing is 'Yours faithfully'.

fib.questionText: The written record of what is discussed and decided at a meeting is called the _____.
fib.explanation: Minutes record the proceedings and decisions of a meeting.

fib.questionText: The list of items to be discussed at a meeting, circulated before it begins, is the _____.
fib.explanation: An agenda sets out, in order, the matters to be dealt with during a meeting.

fib.questionText: A short internal message sent within an organisation, using the headings To, From, Date and Subject, is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A memo (memorandum) is used for internal communication within an organisation.

fib.questionText: A document summarising a person's education, experience and skills for a job application is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A curriculum vitae (CV) gives a summary of an applicant's background for employment purposes.

fib.questionText: A report usually ends with a section giving suggestions for action, called the _____.
fib.explanation: The recommendations section of a report advises what should be done based on the findings.

fib.questionText: A short public message displayed on a board to inform many people is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A notice gives brief, clear information to the public or to a group of people.

fib.questionText: The first heading or part of a report, which states its name or purpose, is the _____.
fib.explanation: A report begins with a title that tells the reader what the report is about.

fib.questionText: The level of formality of language used for a particular purpose and audience is known as the _____.
fib.explanation: Register refers to choosing language that is formal or informal to suit the purpose and audience.

fib.questionText: A card sent to ask someone to attend an event such as a wedding or graduation is called an _____.
fib.explanation: An invitation requests the presence of a guest at a particular event, stating the date, time and place.

tf.questionText: A memo is normally used for communication between organisations rather than within the same organisation.
tf.explanation: A memo is used for internal communication within the same organisation; letters or emails are used between different organisations.

tf.questionText: The agenda is prepared before a meeting, while the minutes are written during or after it.
tf.explanation: The agenda is circulated in advance to plan the meeting; the minutes record what actually happens.

tf.questionText: Informal letters should use formal expressions such as 'I am writing to inform you' and 'Yours faithfully'.
tf.explanation: Informal letters use friendly, relaxed language and personal closings, not formal expressions.

tf.questionText: When the writer knows and uses the recipient's name in a formal letter, the correct closing is 'Yours sincerely'.
tf.explanation: 'Yours sincerely' is used when the greeting names the recipient (e.g. 'Dear Mr Juma').

tf.questionText: A telegram is written in full, detailed sentences to make the message very clear.
tf.explanation: A telegram is brief and often leaves out small words to save space, while still keeping the meaning clear.

tf.questionText: A good notice should be short, clear and contain only the essential information.
tf.explanation: Notices must be concise and clear so that readers grasp the message quickly.

tf.questionText: The purpose and audience of a piece of writing help the writer decide on the correct format and register.
tf.explanation: Both the purpose (why) and the audience (who) determine the appropriate format and level of formality.

tf.questionText: A CV and an application letter usually serve the same purpose, so only one of them is ever needed.
tf.explanation: They work together but differ: the application letter introduces the applicant and states interest, while the CV provides the detailed summary of qualifications.

tf.questionText: The findings section of a report presents the facts or information that were discovered.
tf.explanation: Findings set out what was observed or learned, before the conclusion and recommendations.

tf.questionText: When filling in a form, it is acceptable to ignore the instructions and answer in any way you like.
tf.explanation: Forms must be completed by following the instructions and giving accurate, relevant information in the correct spaces.

summary.questionText: State the four standard headings used at the top of a memo.
summary.explanation: These four headings identify the recipient, sender, date and topic of an internal memo.

summary.questionText: Briefly explain the difference between an agenda and the minutes of a meeting.
summary.correctAnswer: An agenda lists what will be discussed and is prepared before a meeting; the minutes record what was discussed and decided during the meeting.
summary.explanation: The agenda plans the meeting in advance while the minutes are the written record of the proceedings.

summary.questionText: List the main sections normally found in a report.
summary.correctAnswer: Title, introduction, findings, conclusion and recommendations.
summary.explanation: These sections organise a report from its subject through to the suggested action.

summary.questionText: Explain when to use 'Yours faithfully' and when to use 'Yours sincerely' in a formal letter.
summary.correctAnswer: Use 'Yours faithfully' when you do not name the recipient (e.g. Dear Sir/Madam) and 'Yours sincerely' when you use the recipient's name (e.g. Dear Mr Kweka).
summary.explanation: The closing depends on whether the greeting names the recipient.

summary.questionText: Give two main differences between formal and informal letters.
summary.correctAnswer: Formal letters use polite, formal language and a set layout with addresses and formal closings, while informal letters use friendly, relaxed language and personal closings.
summary.explanation: The key differences lie in language/register and the conventions of greeting and closing.

summary.questionText: What is the purpose of a CV, and name three kinds of information it usually contains?
summary.correctAnswer: A CV summarises an applicant's background for a job; it usually contains personal details, education/qualifications and work experience (also skills and referees).
summary.explanation: A CV gives an employer an organised summary of the applicant.

summary.questionText: Why must the purpose and audience be considered before writing any functional text?
summary.correctAnswer: Because they determine the correct format, layout and register so that the message suits why it is written and who will read it.
summary.explanation: Matching format and register to purpose and audience makes the writing effective and appropriate.

summary.questionText: Describe two features that make a good notice.
summary.correctAnswer: It is short and clear, and it contains only the essential information (such as what, when and where), often with a heading.
summary.explanation: Notices must communicate quickly, so brevity and clarity are essential.

summary.questionText: Why are telegrams and short messages written briefly?
summary.correctAnswer: To save space and cost, non-essential words are left out so that only the key message remains.
summary.explanation: Brevity keeps the message economical while still understandable.

summary.questionText: Mention two pieces of information that an invitation card should always include.
summary.correctAnswer: The date and time of the event and the place (venue); it should also state the occasion and who is invited.
summary.explanation: An invitation must tell the guest what the event is and exactly where and when to attend.

hoq.questionText: The headmaster wants to tell all teachers about a sudden staff meeting later the same day. Which format and feature combination is the most suitable?

options.text: A formal application letter with a CV attached
An internal memo with To, From, Date and Subject lines stating the meeting time and venue
A personal letter beginning 'My dear teachers' and ending 'Your loving friend'
Minutes recording what the teachers will decide

hoq.explanation: A memo is the correct format for quick internal communication within an organisation; it uses the headings To, From, Date and Subject and states the essential details. Minutes are written after a meeting, and the letters use the wrong register.

hoq.questionText: A student writes: 'Hey boss! Gimme a job ASAP, I'm super cool and you won't regret it!!!' in an application letter. What is the main problem and the best correction?

options.text: The handwriting is untidy; the student should type the letter
The register is too informal; it should use polite, formal language such as 'I wish to apply for the post of...'
The letter is too long; it should be shortened to one line
The letter lacks pictures; it should include photographs

hoq.explanation: An application letter addresses an employer and must use a formal, polite register. Slang, exclamation marks and casual phrases like 'Hey boss' are inappropriate and should be replaced with professional language.

hoq.questionText: A class secretary must produce a document showing, in order, the topics the class committee will discuss next week, including 'Apologies', 'Confirmation of previous minutes' and 'Any other business'. Which document is being prepared, and what is its role?

options.text: Minutes, which record decisions already made at the meeting
A notice, which simply announces that a meeting will take place
An agenda, which lists in order the items to be discussed before the meeting is held
A report, which gives findings and recommendations after an investigation

hoq.explanation: Items such as 'Apologies', 'Confirmation of previous minutes' and 'Any other business' are standard agenda items listed in order before a meeting. The agenda guides the meeting, whereas minutes record what happens during it.
